title: SLO Governance: Product Alignment & Capacity Commitment Framework
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines a repeatable governance process to align product roadmaps with SLO commitments and capacity allocations. It codifies how feature teams request SLO changes, how SRE evaluates capacity impact, and how error-budget reconciliation is performed quarterly and on-demand. The goal is to reduce SLO drift, avoid surprise capacity shortfalls, and create clear tradeoffs between new feature delivery and reliability.

Scope:
- Applies to all externally visible latency and availability SLOs served by Redwood production clusters (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private control plane proxies).
- Includes multi-tenant routing impacts, burst capacity commitments, and model onboarding windows.
- Does NOT cover internal-only metrics (developer tooling telemetry) unless they affect customer-facing SLAs.

Motivation and objectives:
- Provide an auditable process that links product roadmap milestones to capacity commitments and SLO changes.
- Ensure capacity procurement or reallocation decisions are taken with explicit error-budget risk assessment.
- Make tradeoffs explicit: for each new capability, either increase capacity, accept higher cost-per-token, or accept reduced SLO target for a bounded period.

Key definitions:
- SLO Owner: the service/product engineering manager who owns the customer-facing contract.
- Error Budget: (1 - SLO_target) expressed as allowable unavailability or latency breach over a rolling 28-day window.
- Capacity Commitment: reserved GPU/CPU/IO units allocated to a service for a quarter (committed or burstable).
- Roadmap Impact Review (RIR): a formal review between Product and SRE for any planned change that will materially increase request volume or tail latency (>10% expected demand or >5% tail-latency increase estimate).

Governance principles (top-level):
- All SLO changes that impact customers must go through RIR and be recorded in the SLO Registry.
- Capacity decisions are fiscalized: cost delta and procurement lead time must be captured before approval.
- Error budgets are reconciled at least every quarter; high-burn (>2x expected) triggers immediate remediation.
- Product and SRE accept explicit contracts: either increased capacity, temporary reduced feature rate, or temporary SLO relaxation with clear mitigations.

Process overview (fast path and full path):
1) Fast path (minor changes):
   - Small feature toggles that are estimated to change traffic by <5% or not affect p99 latency.
   - Product files a Change Note and SRE signs off within 3 business days.
   - No procurement required; SLO Registry entry updated.
2) Full path (major changes or model onboarding):
   - Product triggers a Roadmap Impact Review 6 weeks before launch.
   - SRE runs a capacity impact estimation using the Capacity Estimator tool and baseline telemetry.
   - Finance and Procurement are notified if new capacity >10% of current committed pool.
   - Decision: Approve with procurement timeline, Approve with temporary throttles/fallbacks, or Reject (require redesign).

Capacity impact estimation (template):
- Inputs required: expected QPS per route, expected average tokens per request, p50/p90/p99 token latencies, KV cache hit-rate, batch size distribution, model variant (fp16, int8), expected concurrency.
- Estimation output: peak GPU-minutes per day, recommended reserved instances, expected cost delta (USD/month), time-to-procure (days).

Capacity commitment matrix (example):
| Commitment Tier | Typical p99 target | Expected cost delta | Procurement lead | Owner signoff |
|-----------------|--------------------|---------------------|------------------|---------------|
| Tier A (Baseline) | p99 <= 300ms       | +0–5%               | 0–7 days         | SRE Manager   |
| Tier B (Reserved) | p99 <= 250ms       | +5–25%              | 14–45 days       | Infra PM      |
| Tier C (Dedicated) | p99 <= 200ms      | +25%+               | 30–90 days       | Platform Eng  |

Error-budget reconciliation (quarterly + on-demand):
1) Quarterly review: SLO Owners and SRE run the Error Budget Reconciliation meeting. Required artifacts: 28-day burn charts, capacity utilization dashboards, recent incidents, and pending roadmap items.
2) On-demand triggers (immediate reconciliation):
   - Burn rate > 2x expected for 7 consecutive days.
   - Any incident that caused >25% of 28-day error budget consumption.
   - Model onboarding spike where observed token cost exceeds estimate by >15%.
3) Reconciliation outcomes (choose one):
   - Funding: allocate emergency reserved capacity (requires Finance signoff for >$Xk/month).
   - Mitigation: feature throttles, degrade non-critical paths, enable lower-cost quantized model variant.
   - Acceptance: deliberate SLO relaxation for a bounded window (requires exec sponsor).

Runbook: Immediate capacity shortfall (field playbook)
1) Pager to SRE Oncall (primary) — include product PM if feature release is live.
2) Run capacity triage checklist:
   - Verify real-time dashboards (Capacity Utilization, Token Queue depth, Batch sizes, p99 latency).
   - Identify traffic source (tenant, route, model variant).
   - If single-tenant spike: apply token-priority gating for that tenant for 15 minutes; notify account team.
   - If multi-tenant degradation: enable global fallback model and increase batching aggressiveness.
3) Short-term controls (<= 60 minutes):
   - Route-level throttles: 10–30% reduction incremental until error budget burn stabilizes.
   - Toggle lower-precision quantized runtime (int8) for non-critical endpoints.
4) Longer-term remediation (next 72 hours):
   - Plan procurement for Tier B/C if demand sustains.
   - Run root cause analysis and update SLO Registry with any accepted changes.

Operational tooling and dashboards (required telemetry):
- SLO Registry (single source of truth): fields include SLO target, owner, routes covered, change history, linked roadmap ticket.
- Capacity Estimator: python CLI and hosted service; accepts CSV input and returns GPU-minute estimates. Example command:
  $ capacity-estimator --input launch-traffic.csv --model llama-13b --precision fp16 --cache-hit 0.72
- Error Budget Dashboard: 28-day burn rate, contributor incidents, per-tenant burn breakdown.
- Admission Controller (policy): enforces fast-path vs full-path and blocks merges that change public routes without RIR tag.

SLO change template (to be filed in SLO Registry):
- Title: <short name>
- Affected routes: <list>
- Current SLO: <e.g., 99.9% availability p99 <= 300ms>
- Proposed change: <e.g., 99.7% for 2 weeks>
- Motivation: <release, onboarding, cost tradeoff>
- Capacity delta estimate: <GPU-min/day; $/month>
- Rollout plan and rollback criteria: <canary %, triggers>
- Approvals: Product, SRE, Finance (if cost delta > $5k/mo)

Escalation and decision matrix:
- SRE Manager: approve fast-path changes and small capacity reallocations (<10% pool).
- Infra PM: approve reserved commitments (10–25%).
- Head of Platform: approve dedicated or multi-region commitments (>25%) and executive SLO relaxations.
- Exec sponsor required for any SLO relaxation that affects customer SLAs for >14 days.

Templates and artifacts (links and checklist):
- Pre-launch RIR checklist (required): traffic estimate, perf regression lint, evacuation strategy, canary plan.
- SLO Registry entry template (copy for use).
- Capacity Estimator CSV schema (fields documented in Appendix).

Appendix: metrics and query examples
- 28-day error budget burn (PromQL):
  sum(increase(request_breach_total[28d])) / sum(increase(request_total[28d]))
- p99 latency by route:
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- GPU-minute estimate quick check (psuedo-calculation):
  daily_gpu_minutes = peak_qps * avg_tokens * token_ms / 60000 * concurrency_factor
